name: NULL Pointer Dereference
principle: The product dereferences a pointer or reference that it expects to be valid but is NULL. This usually crashes the process and can rarely allow memory access or code execution when address 0 is accessible to privileged code.
detection_signals: malloc/calloc/realloc/strdup/new(std::nothrow) return value used with ->, *, [], memcpy, strcpy, or memset before NULL check
gethostbyaddr/getenv/fopen/dlopen/dlsym return value dereferenced or passed to a dereferencing API before NULL check
Java System.getProperty/Map.get/Intent.getStringExtra return value used with .trim(), .length(), .equals(), or other method before null check
function parameter of pointer/reference type dereferenced with p->field, *p, p[i], or p.method() with no entry null guard and callers can pass NULL/null
callee may return NULL on error path and caller immediately dereferences result or passes it to another function that dereferences it
check occurs after first use: p->field or *p appears before if (p == NULL), if (!p), or Objects.requireNonNull(p)
shared pointer checked for NULL outside a lock and dereferenced later after unlock or without synchronization
negative_signals: if (p == NULL) return/goto/throw occurs before every dereference on the same path
pointer is assigned from &local, &global, array name, or string literal immediately before use
Java reference is validated by Objects.requireNonNull(x) or explicit x != null guard before method call
C++ object is held by reference, gsl::not_null, std::optional checked with has_value(), or smart pointer checked before operator->
caller-side contract enforces non-null and all call sites pass &object, non-null allocation result, or already-checked value
false_defense_traps: checking errno or error code but still dereferencing a possibly NULL return value
assert(p != NULL) used as the only guard when assertions can be compiled out or disabled
input format validation before a lookup API such as gethostbyaddr without checking the lookup result
checking p for NULL after p->field, *p, or p.method() has already executed
checking a shared pointer without holding the lock through both check and dereference
verification_focus: Can NULL/null reach any dereference, method call, field access, array access, or dereferencing library call on the same execution path?

consequence_chains.trigger: a function that can return NULL fails and its return value is not checked
consequence_chains.consequence: process crash or denial of service

consequence_chains.trigger: another thread changes or frees a shared pointer between the NULL check and the dereference
consequence_chains.consequence: crash, unsafe state, or memory corruption

consequence_chains.trigger: excessive allocation request fails and returns NULL before unchecked use

patch_principle: Check every pointer or reference returned by a nullable API before first use.
On NULL/null, return, throw a controlled exception, use a safe default, or jump to cleanup before dereference.
Initialize pointers explicitly and avoid using uninitialized or error-path values.
In concurrent code, hold the proper lock from the NULL check through the final dereference.
Document and enforce non-null function contracts at API boundaries.

minimal_examples.safe: char *p = getenv("HOME"); if (p == NULL) return; printf("%c", p[0]);
